title: The prototype chain and __proto__ versus Object.getPrototypeOf
hook: When JavaScript cannot find a property on an object, it walks a hidden link to another object and keeps looking. That link is the prototype chain — the real mechanism behind inheritance, method sharing, and why `class` is only syntactic sugar.

blocks.text: Every ordinary object has an internal link called **[[Prototype]]** (exposed as `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)`). When you read `obj.toString`, the engine first checks **own properties** on `obj`; if missing, it follows [[Prototype]] to the parent object and repeats until it finds the property or reaches `null`. Constructor functions have a `.prototype` object; instances created with `new` get that object as their [[Prototype]].

entries.plainDefinition: The hidden slot pointing to another object used for property lookup. Not the same as the .prototype property on functions.
Legacy accessor to [[Prototype]]. Prefer Object.getPrototypeOf / Object.setPrototypeOf in new code.
entries.example: `obj.__proto__ === Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` — usually true on ordinary objects.

entries.plainDefinition: An object attached to constructor functions. Becomes the [[Prototype]] of instances created with new.
A property stored directly on the object, not inherited from the chain.
entries.example: `Object.hasOwn(obj, 'id')` returns true for own keys only.

blocks.text: The prototype chain is how JavaScript shares methods without copying them onto every instance. It is also how **polymorphism** works: calling `handler.parse(raw)` looks up `parse` on the instance, then on the constructor prototype, then up the chain. Unlike C# virtual dispatch through a fixed method table, prototype links can be **mutated at runtime** — which is powerful and dangerous.

blocks.title: Two different "prototype" words
blocks.body: `Function.prototype` (a property on functions) is not the same as an object's `[[Prototype]]` (the inheritance link). `new Fn()` wires the instance's [[Prototype]] to `Fn.prototype`.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Check own properties
items.body: The engine searches the object's own keys (including non-enumerable and symbol keys per the operation).

items.title: Follow [[Prototype]]
items.body: If not found, repeat on the prototype object — typically `Constructor.prototype`, then possibly `Object.prototype`.

items.title: Stop at null
items.body: When [[Prototype]] is `null`, lookup returns `undefined` (for reads) or allows defining an own property (for writes).

items.title: Assignment creates own properties
items.body: `obj.x = 1` always creates or updates an **own** property on `obj` — it does not walk the chain to assign on a parent (unless the parent has a setter).

blocks.title: Replacing constructor.prototype breaks instanceof
blocks.body: If you assign `AuthHandler.prototype = {}` after instances exist, old instances still point at the old prototype object. New instances use the new one — `instanceof` becomes inconsistent.

blocks.title: Confusing .prototype with [[Prototype]]
blocks.body: Only functions have `.prototype` by default. An instance's inheritance link is [[Prototype]], accessed via `Object.getPrototypeOf(instance)`.

blocks.text: Engines optimize prototype lookup with **hidden classes** (Shapes in V8). When you mutate [[Prototype]] with `Object.setPrototypeOf` or delete/add properties aggressively, you can deoptimize to dictionary mode — measurable on hot loops. **Property shadowing**: an own property hides an inherited one without deleting the parent copy. **Setters on the chain**: assignment `obj.x = v` invokes a setter on a prototype if no own property exists — unlike C# field assignment. **class** desugars to the same prototype wiring: `class A extends B` sets `A.prototype`'s [[Prototype]] to `B.prototype`. There is no separate virtual table — interviewers want you to say **mutable prototype lookup**, not C#-style vtables.

snippet.explanation: Line 6: assignment creates own `role` on admin. Line 8: changing prototype affects instances without own shadow. Line 11–12: shadowing vs shared mutation — classic interview scenario.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying JavaScript has virtual methods like C# — lookup is prototype-based and mutable. Claiming __proto__ is the standard API — prefer getPrototypeOf. Thinking assignment walks up the chain to write on parents — it creates own properties unless a setter intercepts.

interviewTakeaways: Property lookup checks own properties first, then walks [[Prototype]] until null.
Function.prototype becomes the [[Prototype]] of instances created with new; class extends wires the same links.
__proto__ is legacy; use Object.getPrototypeOf and Object.setPrototypeOf.

60s: JS inheritance is a prototype chain — linked objects, not a CLR type table. Methods live on constructor.prototype. Lookup is dynamic and mutable. instanceof checks prototype linkage. class is syntactic sugar over the same mechanism.
Follow-up: what happens if you replace Constructor.prototype after creating instances?
commonPitfalls: Weak: 'class creates a new inheritance system.' Strong: class desugars to prototype wiring — same [[Prototype]] links.
Confusing function.prototype (property on functions) with object [[Prototype]] (inheritance link on instances).
Mutating shared .prototype in libraries — affects all instances without own shadow properties.

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# override uses a fixed vtable slot; JS method call is prototype property lookup that can change at runtime.
TypeScript classes compile to constructor functions and prototype assignment — types erase, chain remains.
